characters: A cheerful child in a school uniform showing fingers and toes, with a friend.

narrationPlan.voice: Playful voice; numbers said a little louder
narrationPlan.pace: Bouncy and slow enough to count on fingers (about 70 words per minute)
notes: Read dialogue with a different voice for each character.
Pause for two seconds at each question activity.
Never rush the last page: let the ending land.

music: A bouncy tune on a small drum, going up one note for each number (placeholder)
culturalNotes: Counting rhymes on fingers are used in many languages. This one is original. Teachers can count in Twi, Ga, Ewe or the school’s language too.
reviewQuestions: Is the language right for the stated age band and reading level?
Is anything here inaccurate, stereotyped or unsafe for children?
Check the counting and that the hand-washing line is clear.

teacherGuide.overview: A counting rhyme to ten. Form: five couplets. Rhyming pairs: five/alive, ten/again (slant), day/play, high/hi, one/done. It teaches counting, rhyme and hand-washing.
whileReading: Hold up the right number of fingers.
afterReading: Count ten objects and put them in two groups of five.
Count to ten in a home language.
discussion: When do we wash our hands?
reflection: What do your hands help you do?

mathsExtension.task: Show 6 fingers. How many more to make 10?

stretch: Count in twos to ten on fingers.

culturalNotes: Counting rhymes on fingers are used in many languages. This one is original. Teachers can count in Twi, Ga, Ewe or the school’s language too.
localiseThis: Add counting words from the children’s home languages.
